text:
I fixed six bugs in `catalog/` so the code matches the tests. I couldn't run `python3 -m unittest` because I don't have a shell here, so the suite hasn't been run. I checked each fix against the test that exercises it by reading the code.

- **`fees.py`**: the late fee added `DAILY_FEE` to the number of days late instead of multiplying, so 1 day late cost 1.25 instead of 0.25. It now multiplies.
- **`members.py`**: `MAX_BORROWED` was 3, but the comment and the tests say 5. Set it to 5.
- **`inventory.py`**: `recent(n)` sliced `[-n-1:]`, which returned one event too many. It now uses `[-n:]`, and returns `[]` when `n` is 0 or less. That last part is my own choice; no test covers it.
- **`factory.py`**: the sample catalog was missing `Emma`. I added `Book("Emma", "Austen", 1815, 1)`. The tests only check the title, so the author, year and copy count are values I picked.
- **`books.py`**: `parse_book` kept the year as a string, which also broke `age()`. It now converts it with `int(year)`.
- **`search.py`**: it imported `normalize` from a module that doesn't exist (`catalog.nonexistent`). It now imports it from `catalog.text`.

Please run `python3 -m unittest` to confirm everything passes.
